newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore construction contracts hit S$17 bln - minister.
newsitem.headline: Singapore construction contracts hit S$17 bln - minister.

text.p: New construction contracts awarded in Singapore will probably reach Singapore $17 billion for 1996, Minister for Labour Lee Boon Yang said on Tuesday.
Speaking at the opening of the second international congress on construction, Lee said the value of contracts awarded this year would be six percent more than last year.
The increase also "indicates that construction growth is likely to be sustained for the next two years", he said.
Lee noted that while the industry is seeing good growth, overall construction productivity has been declining since November 1992.
This conincided with the government's move in 1992 to let contractors recruit more foreign workers to ease the tight labour market, Lee said.
"Unfortunately, it resulted in the industry taking the easiest option to cope with growing demand. More and more foreign construction workers were brought in to sustain the industry," he said.
This has led to lower productivity: in the second quarter of this year, construction productivity fell by 10.4 percent, the minister said.
